topic: How the Apollo 13 crew made it home

storylines.title: They Didn't Just Turn Around
storylines.pitch: Everyone assumes that after the explosion the crew simply flew back. But Apollo 13 had already left its safe return path to aim for the Moon. Ground controllers computed a 35-second burn of a landing engine, fired five hours later, to put them back on course.
storylines.conflict: The explosion vented both oxygen tanks, and the ship was on a course that no longer led safely home.
storylines.stakes: The ship was nearly 200,000 miles out, the crew had to move into the lunar module lifeboat, and the course had to be fixed fast.
storylines.twist: The engine that saved them was the lunar module descent engine, the one built for the landing they never made.
storylines.payoff: No U-turn was possible; a 35-second burn from the lander got them back onto a free-return course.

storylines.title: 3 Fixes That Brought Apollo 13 Home
storylines.pitch: After an oxygen tank explosion far from Earth, the crew survived on three fixes. Number three was a 35-second engine burn, number two was a lander turned lifeboat, and number one was plastic bags, cardboard and tape.
storylines.conflict: With both oxygen tanks ruptured, the crew had to get home using whatever they had.
storylines.stakes: Each fix is more improvised than the last, ending with a repair built only from materials already on board.
storylines.twist: The biggest fix was a connector for the canisters, made from plastic bags, cardboard and tape.
storylines.payoff: The countdown shows that bags, cardboard and tape helped bring the crew home.

storylines.title: You're 200,000 Miles From Home
storylines.hook: Something just exploded 200,000 miles from home.
storylines.pitch: You're in Apollo 13 when a short circuit blows up an oxygen tank and both tanks vent into space. Your ship is dying, so you move into the lander meant for the Moon, but you're off the course home. The lander's engine fires for 35 seconds, and a fix made from tape and cardboard finishes the job.
storylines.conflict: You're nearly 200,000 miles from Earth after the explosion, and the oxygen is gone.
storylines.stakes: First the oxygen vents, then you learn you're off course, then you need an engine burn and a repair built from what's on board.
storylines.twist: The lander you were going to land on the Moon in becomes your lifeboat.
storylines.payoff: You make it home because of the lander's full oxygen tank and engine, a 35-second burn, and a tape-and-cardboard fix.
